 BarkBoard and Friends Predictions: Fresno State at Texas State
 How will the Fresno State at Texas State game go? See predictions from BarkBoard.com and local media members.
 Jackson Moore 2 
 After falling at Utah State, the Fresno State Bulldogs are now 10-point underdogs at Texas State. Can the 'Dogs bounce back and secure bowl eligibility?  BarkBoard.com and local media partners make their predictions for how they expect the game to play out. 
 Fresno State and Texas State kick off on Saturday at 1:00 p.m. PT at UFCU Stadium in San Marcos. The game will have a nationally televised broadcast on The CW. Texas State has the nation's No. 5 rushing offense at 265.8 yards per game, but is also one of the Pac-12's top passing threats with dual-threat quarterback Brad Jackson running the offense. 
 Fresno State (5-4, 2-3) is yet to be mathematically eliminated from Pac-12 Championship contention, but needs two more wins and some help from the conference. The Bulldogs need a win, for Boise State to defeat Oregon State, and for Utah State to defeat San Diego State, in order to stay alive. Texas State (5-4, 3-2) has only lost two conference games by a combined total of three points, but also needs help to break out of a four-way tie for second place. 
 BarkBoard.com's Jackson Moore is joined by local media partners that each give their take on this week's matchup. On the panel are: Scott Bemis (Sports Anchor for KSEE24 & CBS47, Host of Bulldog Insider), Phil Benotti (Host of Behind the Bench on 1430 ESPN Fresno) and Lucio Ourique (Host of the Red Wave Report Podcast). 
 Jackson Moore - BarkBoard.com
 Fresno State was able to bring the offensive firepower against a ranked Boise State and a high-powered Oregon State. Yet they were gummed up by lesser-perceived teams San Diego State and Utah State teams in the trenches. 
 While it's a step up in competition this week, the Bulldogs do appear to match up better with this style of opponent. Like Boise State, the Bobcats are statistically strong against the run but weak against the pass. I expect the Bulldogs will take a similar approach that they used against Boise State that featured Jayden Mandal attempting 33 passes and the 'Dogs putting up 31 points. 
 However, Texas State's offense will be difficult for Fresno State - or any other defense - to handle. The Bobcats are fifth in the country in rushing yards per game, and they also have one of the top passers in the conference in Brad Jackson. The 'Dogs have not been bad against the run, but haven't been dominant enough defensively to lead wins either. 
 While the 'Dogs had answers for Oregon State's passing attack, Texas State has an additional wrinkle. Jackson's dual-threat makes him the No. 7 rusher in the conference. Running QBs have not burnt the Bulldogs this year but have been able to extend plays and convert third downs. The quarterback threat, balance, and Bobcat running game prove to be too much to slow down. 
 Fresno State's offense will loo  leaps and bounds better than last week, but it's also not enough to out-score the Bobcats. The Bulldogs' path to victory here is similar to that of the Oregon State game: force third- (and fourth-) down stops in the red zone, create turnovers, and find balance on offense. 
 Texas State 31, Fresno State 24 
 Bulldog to Watch: DB Ethan Tierney
 (Photo: Jackson Moore, 247Sports) 
 Fresno State has lost three of its last four games. Out of 16 quarters, the best 5 for the defense have been when Ethan Tierney has been on the field (four vs Oregon State, one before ejected for targeting at Utah State). The Bulldog defense looks a notch better on Saturday with Tierney back on the field. 
 I don't think Fresno State wins this game unless they force a turnover - or two. Simeon Harris is the go-to Bulldog in this department, but he has not had a takeaway in five weeks. Tierney or Harris make a big play in this one. 
 Texas State's Jackson has only two games with multiple sacks and one game with multiple interceptions. The 'Dogs have, however, caused unusual issues for passing attacks by San Jose State and Oregon State that those teams rarely saw previously. 
 Scott Bemis - KSEE24 & CBS47
 I've done a fair amount of research the last two weeks before giving my predictions, and have been wrong both weeks, predicting Oregon State to take down the Bulldogs, and the 'Dogs to beat Utah State. 
 So, this week I'm just going more with my gut. And my gut is telling me the Bulldogs are due for a bounce back effort against Texas State. 
 Considering the Fresno State captains and team leaders met with Coach Entz for over an hour after getting back from Logan, I get the sense this team is practicing with a little edge this week, and that the 'Dogs will come out with something to prove Saturday in San Marcos. 
 That by itself, doesn't guarantee the Bulldogs will get a win, especially when you take into account the Bobcats might be playing as good a football as anybody in the league (including Boise State) over the last several weeks. 
 But this feels like a buy low spot on the Bulldogs, and a sell high spot on the Bobcats.
 I think the 'Dogs are better than they showed last week in Logan, and the Bobcats might be due for a little bit of a letdown here, after playing consecutive road games at high-profile Pac-12 teams Boise State and Oregon State. 
 Like in Fresno State's game against the Beavers, I think the Bulldog defense will rise to the challenge of facing an explosive offense, and DC Nick Benedetto will at least find a way to slow them down a little bit, and probably generate a couple turnovers against a Bobcat squad that has turned it over 13 times in their first nine games. 
 The Bulldog offense meantime, will take advantage of a Bobcat pass defense that gives up nearly 300 yards a game, and find a way to get in the end zone three or four times, allowing this one to stay close late into the fourth quarter, where Bulldog kicker Manaki Watanabe will have his first chance to make a game-winning field goal, and he will deliver. 
 Fresno State 30, Texas State 28 
 Bulldog to Watch: WR Ezekiel Avit
 (Photo: Jackson Moore, 247Sports) 
 Since Zeke exploded for six catches for 96 yards and two receiving touchdowns against Boise State, he has gone quiet the last three games, only producing six catches total for 72 yards over that span, even though he did find the end zone late last week against Utah State. 
 There are a few reasons why I think he could have a big game.  
 First off, the aforementioned Bobcat pass defense has some holes in it. 
 Secondly, considering Josiah Freeman had the big night at Utah State last week, I could see the Bobcats rolling coverage over to Josiah, which could open up more opportunities for secondary receivers like Avit. 
 Thirdly, Bulldog head coach Matt Entz delivered a subtle message at this week's press conference that it was okay for Jayden Mandal to throw to others besides Freeman, so I think that is something that was probably emphasized at practice this week - getting more people involved, and in that case, Avit seems like the receiver that could be the biggest beneficiary.
 Phil Benotti - 1430 ESPN Fresno
 Fresno State had more ups and downs than any season I can remember, and if there's a silver lining coming into this game, it's that they're due for a good game. Texas State presents plenty of challenges on both sides of the ball, but nothing that a good version of this Bulldogs can't overcome. The emphasis on offense is how quick of a start can they get in this one. Fresno State has scored just 3 points combined in the 1 st  quarter of all five of their road games thus far. It baffles me that this team has that much of a disparity when it comes to road and home offensive splits. It's their last chance to change the narrative, and I think they can do it if they trust the playmakers that got them there. Josiah Freeman has been awesome all year, but Speedy Luke and Zeke Avit are names that have been too quiet on the stat sheet lately.
 On the flip side, this defense will need to come up big against a high-power rushing attack. No turnovers against Utah State killed any chance of flipping the energy and momentum of that game, and I think this will be a huge factor in San Marcos. If the Bulldogs can flip it to a short field for the offense and give them good chances to score, then that's when Fresno State can play their best. The front seven will have to show up big in this one, and I look forward to seeing if they are up to the challenge in this one. There's a reason they are ranking in the top of the conference in defensive statistics.
 Fresno State 30, Texas State 28 
 Bulldog to Watch: QB Jayden Mandal
 (Photo: Jackson Moore, 247Sports) 
 It always seems to rest on the shoulders of a quarterback to pull a team out of a slump. Jayden will need to be sharp to do so, but I think it's possible on the road. He has to trust his line to protect him and look at all the options he has to throw to. Plus, navigating in the run game and setting up his offense to be in the right places will be massive if the Bulldogs want to be balanced in their attack. It's a big prove it game for everyone on offense, and I hope that the QB can be the one to deliver a surprising upset.
 Lucio Ourique - Red Wave Report Podcast
 Texas State has the offensive firepower to pull away at home in San Marcos, though Fresno State's disciplined defense and ball security should keep this Pac-12 matchup competitive into the fourth quarter.
 While Texas State stifles the run (114.7 YPG allowed), its pass defense surrenders 292.2 yards per game. Fresno State is coming off a sluggish 17–10 loss at Utah State where the offense stalled, so Mandal will need to take advantage of soft coverage downfield and keep drives alive with backs Bryson Donelson and Rayshon Luke.
 Texas State is 4–1 at UFCU Stadium this season and enters off a dominant 41-21 road win at Oregon State. Fresno State's defense is physical enough to prevent a blowout and keep the Bulldogs within striking distance — making the Bulldogs' 9.5 underdog line and the under of 59.5 attractive outlooks — but Texas State's tempo and red-zone efficiency (25 touchdowns in 30 trips) give the Bobcats the edge late.
 Texas State 31, Fresno State 24 
 Bulldog to Wwtch: WR Josiah Freeman
 (Photo: Andrew Wevers, Getty) 
 If Fresno State keeps pace, look for quarterback Jayden Mandal to target his top receiver early and often against a Texas State secondary surrendering 292.2 passing yards per game (137th in FBS). Freeman leads the Bulldogs with 45 catches for 626 yards and 4 touchdowns and has the vertical speed to exploit single coverage downfield.
 Las Vegas Oddsmakers
 Fresno State is a 10-point road underdog at Texas State. The over/under score total is set at 59.5 points. That makes for a projected scorer of about 35-25. 
 BarkBoard Message Board Predictions
 BarkBoard message board posters have also made their score predictions for the game. Read them and post your own prediction on the forum here:   https://247sports.com/college/fresno-state/board/102987/contents/score-predictions-fresno-state-at-texas-state-292638397/   
 About the Panel
 Jackson Moore - Moore has spent the past 17 seasons covering Fresno State football for BarkBoard.com. He also contributes to the 247Sports network covering college football recruiting on the Oregon Ducks beat. 
 Scott Bemis - Bemis has been with KSEE24 and CBS47 since 2014. He is the evening sports anchor on newscasts, co-hosts CBS47 Sidelines on Fridays, and hosts the Bulldog Insider on KSEE24 on Sunday nights. BarkBoard's Moore can be seen as a guest on the Bulldog Insider each Sunday this season. 
 Phil Benotti - Benotti is the host of Behind The Bench on ESPN 1430 weekdays from 3 to 6 p.m. PT. BarkBoard's Moore can be heard as a guest on the Behind The Bench show, as well as on ESPN 1430's Sportsline: The Bulldog Hour with Tony D. The Bulldog Hour airs weekdays at 2 p.m. PT, with Moore scheduled for Tuesdays and Thursdays this season.
 Lucio Ourique - Ourique is the long-time host of the Red Wave Report Podcast, having covered Fresno State football for over a decade. BarkBoard's Moore can be heard on the weekly podcast on all platforms where podcasts can be found.
